business.name: Fieldview Acres Mercantile / Newton Falls Treasure Hunt

evidence.observedFact: Organizer Tom Colosimo said he intends to run the treasure hunt again the following year and may expand it into the township or surrounding communities because it benefits local businesses.
The 2026 hunt concluded July 9 with a prize valued above $37,650 after drawing large numbers of visitors into Newton Falls over roughly five months.
The hunt grew beyond 60 sponsors and was explicitly designed to bring people into Newton Falls businesses.

A participating restaurant reported sales increases on clue-drop days, showing the hunt generated measurable traffic but not, from the public evidence reviewed, a unified participant-retention and merchant-attribution layer after visits.

gaps.recommendedFix: Position Places Rewards as the participant-retention layer for the next hunt: permissioned participant capture, return-visit rewards, merchant-specific offers, referrals, and post-hunt lifecycle campaigns.

Create a shared sponsor/merchant attribution system that tracks which participating businesses receive hunt traffic and automatically follows participants into measurable repeat visits after clue drops and after the hunt ends.
Add trackable participant referrals and cross-business discovery so the next hunt compounds its audience instead of relying only on clue drops and social reach.

recommendedEntryOffer: 2027 Newton Falls Treasure Hunt Operating System
notes: Treat 2027 as an organizer-stated intention, not a formally scheduled event, until dates are publicly announced. Pitch Places Rewards before sponsor and merchant mechanics are finalized. Lead with participant retention, sponsor/merchant attribution, post-hunt conversion, referral growth and measurable merchant ROI. Do not claim that the organizer currently lacks any private CRM or tracking system without validating it directly.
